claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning a new assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**What is the age of the child you want to claim Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know:
- The name(s) of your child/children
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for your help! I'm inquiring about my son Alex. He's 9 years old and lives at home with me here in the UK. I just want to make sure I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It sounds like Alex is 9 years old, which means he falls into the under 16 age category. That's a good start!

Let me continue with the assessment. Since Alex is under 16, I need to check one important thing:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Alex's age means he qualifies for the initial eligibility check. Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 9 years old, I expect the answer is that he's not in paid work, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 9! He's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I'd expect for a 9-year-old. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check another eligibility requirement:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?** 

Specifically, I'm asking whether Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

(These are benefits someone might receive if they had a disability or health condition, but at age 9 in primary school, this is unlikely to be the case.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 9-year-old at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check the apprenticeship status:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship, or is he just in full-time education at primary school?**

Given that Alex is 9 years old and in primary school, I expect he's not in any apprenticeship, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's definitely not in an apprenticeship - he's just 9 and in primary school! That's years away for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That makes sense. Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency status, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you meet UK residency requirements?** Here are the main ways you could qualify:

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the simplest path
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status and are working** - earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months
4. **You have pre-settled status and actively seeking work** - looking for work (can claim as jobseeker for up to 91 days)
5. **You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources** - financially supporting yourself and your family (and not claiming certain benefits)
6. **You have pre-settled status and are studying** - studying with sufficient resources to support yourself
7. **You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national**
8. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** - in a qualifying country

Since you mentioned you live in the UK with Alex, can you confirm: **Do you normally live in the UK?** If so, that satisfies the residency requirement!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - we both live here together.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That confirms you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm that you are responsible for Alex. This typically means one of the following:

1. **You live with the child** - which you've already mentioned is the case
2. **You contribute to the child's upkeep** - paying for things like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, or presents
3. **You're paying maintenance** - under a court order or agreement for the child's care

Since you've already told me you live with Alex at home in the UK, you clearly meet the responsibility requirement.

Can you confirm: **You live with Alex and contribute to his care and upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me and I provide for all his needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear. Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check one important detail:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is a grandparent or other family member claiming for him?
- Has someone else already started a claim for Alex?

This is important because only one person can receive Child Benefit for each child (though if there's an agreement between two eligible people about who should claim, that can be arranged).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him and I haven't claimed it before.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Where does Alex normally live?**

- **In a hospital** - staying in hospital for a prolonged period?
- **In care** - in a local authority care home or similar arrangement?
- **Fostered** - in a fostering arrangement?
- **At home normally** - living with you at home?

Based on what you've told me, I expect Alex lives at home with you, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me normally - just a regular family situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost at the end of the assessment. I have just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- You are fully responsible for paying for his housing, food, and care costs?
- The council is not contributing financially to his upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - I pay for everything myself. The council isn't paying anything towards his care or accommodation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! Let me process your final answer and provide you with the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!**

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

**Child:** Alex (age 9)  
**Status:** ✅ ELIGIBLE

### Why You Qualify:

✓ Alex is under 16 years old  
✓ He is not working full-time  
✓ He does not receive disqualifying benefits (ESA or Universal Credit)  
✓ He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✓ You normally live in the UK (residency requirement met)  
✓ You live with Alex and provide for all his needs (responsibility requirement met)  
✓ No other person is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  
✓ Alex lives at home with you normally  
✓ The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance  

---

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** - Use form CH2 if applying by post
2. **Provide proof of identity** - For both yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth or adoption certificate**
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some of the benefit through tax
5. **Payment frequency** - Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### Useful Links:
- [How to claim Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
- [Child Benefit eligibility](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility)

Congratulations! You should go ahead and make your claim. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
